chapter_title: Chương 47: 0047 【Chia Lợi Nhuận Bốn Vạn Hơn Trong Nửa Tháng】

segments.title: Chương 47: 0047 【Chia Lợi Nhuận Bốn Vạn Hơn Trong Nửa Tháng】
segments.content:
Why did Tao Chenggang want to merge the servers of the first few districts in pairs?

Because the loss of free-to-play players was a bit serious. Not to mention those who abandoned the game directly, some ran to the new districts to create new accounts, and others went to other private servers.

There were three main "other private servers," and all of them used the Abyss dungeon gameplay. They were bona fide copycats.

The first one died quickly, with all sorts of bugs flying everywhere.

The second and third ones, however, were meticulously polished.

Especially the third private server, which advertised something like "get Abyss dungeon entry tickets upon entering the game," was extremely attractive to free-to-play players.

Shanda wasn't Chen Guiliang's enemy; his peers running private servers were!

December 11th, Wednesday.

Day 13 since Abyss Legend went online.

Chen Guiliang was preparing for the monthly exam. He hadn't finished his lunch when he got a call. Chewing on twice-cooked pork, he asked, "Brother Gang, did the lawyer's letter from Shanda arrive?"

"Can't you say something nice for a change?"

Tao Chenggang didn't know whether to laugh or cry. "The server merge originally scheduled for Friday night has been canceled."

"Are new players coming into the game again?" Chen Guiliang was quite surprised.

Tao Chenggang said, "Popular Computer Software's interview with us was published in this month's second issue, which was this Monday. A wave of new players came in that night, and even more came on Tuesday and Wednesday. I estimate it will rise again over the weekend, so there's no hurry to merge the servers and districts."

Although Popular Computer Software magazine had begun to decline, its single-issue circulation was still over 150,000 copies.

Many of its readers had computers at home.

"A pleasant surprise," Chen Guiliang said with a laugh.

Tao Chenggang continued, "I'm also contacting more internet cafes to partner with. Although internet cafe players have a slightly weaker ability to top-up, their presence in the game is great for livening things up. With a large number of internet cafe players around, the whales can have a good time."

After chatting a bit more, Tao Chenggang said, "I'm hanging up. Boss Shi sent me a QQ message!"

Tao Chenggang pocketed his phone, his hands flying across the keyboard as he typed, "Mr. Shi, good afternoon."

"Your private server is still alive? Shanda doesn't seem to care much about you guys."

"They're rich and powerful, they look down on our small operation."

"Have you thought it over? Come and develop a game with me."

"I'll think about it some more."

"Alright. I'll leave you my office number. If you're ever in Modu for a visit, you can call me and we can have a meal..."

"Thank you for your high regard, Mr. Shi. This is my cell phone number..."

Boss Shi had already confirmed that he would go to Jing City next week to sign the contract, selling off Brain Platinum to a friend and 75% of Golden Partner's shares to Sitong Company.

After selling these, he was going to venture into the online gaming market.

As for leaving his number for Tao Chenggang, it was purely a quirk of Boss Shi's personality. He didn't care about status when making friends; what mattered was whether he liked the person. Sometimes, a drink was all it took to become friends.

Even if Tao Chenggang refused to cooperate, he could still go have a meal with Boss Shi.

Twenty years later, Boss Shi would be forced to execute a payment of 1.765 billion yuan, all stemming from his careless habit of acting as a guarantor for others. It was nothing more than having too many motley friends. As long as they had a good time drinking with him, he'd lend millions just like that, signing guarantee contracts on a whim while tipsy.

That's just how casually the figures who rose up from the grassroots era did things.

Saturday.

Abyss Legend's peak concurrent online players reached over 8,600.

Chen Guiliang, on the other hand, was facing his second exam since his rebirth.

The monthly exam.

The first and second-year high school students had the weekend off, which conveniently freed up classrooms for the third-year students to use as exam halls.

The exam numbers were completely random and not arranged according to mid-term results.

Of the guys in dorm 302, only Liu Zhihong was in the same exam room as Chen Guiliang.

"Are you confident?" Chen Guiliang ran into Bian Guanyue in the hallway.

Bian Guanyue said, "It's alright. I've made a lot of progress recently, I've been asking Wu Meng for help with many difficult problems every day. What about you?"

Chen Guiliang said, "I'm alright too."

"Good luck."

"Good luck."

Bian Guanyue was actually a little nervous.

She used to be an arts student, but now she had switched to being a regular student. No matter how hard she worked, it was still difficult to keep up.

This was her first exam since transferring schools.

Chen Guiliang, however, walked into the exam room full of confidence, but the Chinese language paper left him a bit stunned.

He wasn't sure about the very first multiple-choice question (on word pronunciation).

There was also a multiple-choice question in the reading comprehension section. Although he knew which one to choose to get points, he still thought all the options were correct.

The question was not well-written!

There was another question where, from the question-setter's perspective, he knew he had to choose D to get the points. But answer D itself had a logical fallacy of confusing cause and effect.

These situations left Chen Guiliang especially speechless.

He even wanted to curse the question-setter for being an idiot!

He had his math exam in the afternoon.

Chen Guiliang could only skip through the questions. For the topics he hadn't reviewed yet, he was completely clueless and couldn't answer at all.

For the topics he had reviewed, he could solve about seventy to eighty percent of them.

Next was English.

He mostly guessed on the listening comprehension questions.

Alright, he mostly guessed on a lot of the English questions that followed...

Liberal Arts Comprehensive exam.

Chen Guiliang did pretty well on this one. At least he wrote down answers for all the questions.

The two days of exams were over.

The guys in 302 were quite excited, all feeling that they had performed above their usual level.

This could only mean that the monthly exam questions were easy, intentionally designed to boost the students' confidence.

"Great Hero Chen, what score do you think you'll get this time?" Xu Haibo asked.

Chen Guiliang said, "I don't know, I did so-so."

Xie Yang boasted, "I found the questions especially easy this time. I think I can get back to the Tier 1 university admission score."

"I think I can pass the Tier 1 line too," Yang Hao said delightedly.

Yang Hao's scores fluctuated wildly. When the questions were easy, he became more confident as he did them. When they were difficult, he would get nervous. The more anxious he got, the worse he did, even making mistakes on questions he originally knew how to do.

As everyone was lively discussing the monthly exam, Uncle Feng Tao suddenly called.

Chen Guiliang ran outside to find a signal for his PHS phone, and Xie Yang followed him out stealthily.

"Uncle, is there something urgent?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Feng Tao said, "The profits from the private server for the first 15 days have been calculated. Brother Gang put me in charge of the accounting specifically to put your mind at ease."

"The most players top-up on weekends. Especially the day before the fortress siege event, the single-day top-up amount broke 40,000 yuan. Those whales were like madmen, taking their whole guilds to grind dungeons."

"Top-ups are usually lower on weekdays. On low days, it's two or three thousand a day; on high days, it's five or six thousand."

"Over the past half month, the total top-up amount was over 256,000."

"After deducting the private server production costs, platform promotion costs, server rental costs, as well as the internet cafe's cut, bank fees, and employee salaries and bonuses, the four of us partners made a net profit of 158,000."

"Your share is 28%, which comes out to over 44,000. It's already been transferred to your bank account."

Chen Guiliang said cheerfully, "Thanks for your hard work, Uncle."

Feng Tao said dejectedly, "It's no hard work for me, Uncle. Uncle is just full of regret."

"Hahaha!"

Chen Guiliang laughed out loud.

When Feng Tao partnered on the private server, he only made a symbolic investment of 2,000 yuan, so his dividend was practically negligible.

Tao Chenggang gave him an extra three thousand this time, counting it under salary and bonus expenses.

In addition, Tao Chenggang also rented a private residence and set up a few computers as a command center. Tao Chenggang covered these costs himself because the rent wasn't much, and the computers and desks could be moved to the internet cafe.

Chen Guiliang was in a great mood. A half-month dividend of 44,000 yuan!

Moreover, the production cost of the private server had been deducted this one time, so it wouldn't need to be calculated for the next dividend.

From now on, aside from operational costs, the rest would be pure profit.

Feng Tao quickly poured a basin of cold water on him. "This weekend, two more private servers featuring dungeon gameplay went online. One of them was even made by the DuDu Legend team. Our competitors are growing in number!"

"It was bound to happen. We'll just make as much as we can while we can," Chen Guiliang said, rather philosophical about it.

He hung up the phone.

Xie Yang asked impatiently, "Did you get your dividend?"

Chen Guiliang nodded. "Yeah, I got thirty or forty thousand."

"Holy crap, holy crap, holy crap..."

Xie Yang's vocabulary had failed him. Tens of thousands of yuan was an astronomical figure to him.

And Chen Guiliang had earned it in just half a month.

"Let's go, time for evening self-study," Chen Guiliang patted his shoulder.

Xie Yang finally came to his senses. "You damn well better treat us to a meal tomorrow at noon!"

"No problem."

"Plus a pack of Hongtashan."

"Minors shouldn't smoke."

Evening self-study.

The homeroom teacher, Liu Shuying, walked in with the test papers. "I'll announce the English scores directly. The questions on this monthly exam were relatively easy. The class's overall performance has improved compared to the mid-term exam."

"The one most deserving of praise is Peng Yang. He's always been lopsided in his subjects, with his English long hovering around 100 points. Through his hard work, he scored 118 on English this time! Let's give him a round of applause!"

*Clap clap clap clap...*

A sparse round of applause sounded.

Peng Yang's face was flushed, but he was too embarrassed to be smug, so he straightened his back with a serious expression.

"Now I'll hand out the papers, scores from high to low. Wu Meng, 148, first again!"

Wu Meng, like a proud little princess, went to collect her paper with her head held high.

"Li Rui, 145, great improvement."

Li Rui trotted up to get his paper with a grin.

Two minutes later, Liu Shuying said, "Chen Guiliang, 93."

Seeing the teacher's displeased expression, Chen Guiliang said brazenly, "Teacher, I've improved. I only got 82 on the mid-term."

Liu Shuying said irritably, "The monthly exam was easier. You'd better watch yourself. I can't manage you."

"Bian Guanyue, 92. There's still a lot of room for improvement."

Bian Guanyue was very happy. She used to only get scores in the seventies or eighties on English exams. Her efforts recently had clearly paid off.

The next day, the scores for all subjects were announced one after another.

Chen Guiliang's monthly exam results were as follows:

Chinese 136, Math 68, English 93, Politics 75, History 79, Geography 85. (The monthly exam didn't have a comprehensive liberal arts paper; Politics, History, and Geography were all tested as separate subjects.)

Total score: 536.

It seemed like a good score, but because the questions were not difficult, all the students performed well overall.

The school made a rough estimate and drew a few cut-off lines based on the situation.

The cut-off for Tier 2 universities was set at 535 points.

Chen Guiliang had just managed to scrape by on the tail end of the Tier 2 line.
